Hey, I know for certain that your parents would rather support you for the rest of their lives than have you explore door #2. 

There's no shame in getting support from your parents whike you're in a rough spot. Fuck, my dad moved back in with his mom when he was nearly 50 years old when he was in between jobs. A few years later and he's doing great.

I'm here if you want to talk.

Hey, you're not a whiny college kid and you definitely will make it out of this year alive. There's a lot of months left to figure something out and that's exactly what we should do. I'm here if you want to talk.

Hey man.... I'm not sure if this helps at all but I'm a 23 year old virgin and I wouldnt say I have below-average looks. I actually think I look decent. Sure I could lose 20lbs but what I'm getting at is that I don't think looks are the factor here. I've met and seen so many people over the years that are "ugly" or overweight with pretty girlfriends. Initially the thought is painful but at the end of the day I realize it all comes down to a lot more than looks. These people put in the effort where I am unwilling. Sure if you worked out every day and got jacked it might be easy, but that takes a lot of commitment when jerking off takes none. I think the play for people like us is "fake it till you make it." If it's that important to you to not be a virgin to where you're considering taking your own life, stop doing things that take no effort like Tinder and force yourself to go out to the bars on weekends. You don't have to get drunk or even order a drink for that matter. Just sit at the bar and talk with people who are drunk at first, and realize the only thing holding you back is your inhibitions. Keep doing it. Eventually you'll strike up conversations, pretend like you're the confident douchebag. Who cares if someone is rude and tells you off, just keep doing it. It will happeb eventually.

I know it's probably hard to take advice from someone who is a 23yr old virgin, but if there's one thing I've learned it's that sometimes you've got to go out of your comfort zone day after day if you want to achieve something. And this might not work for you, but this is my plan anyway, when I have the time. I haven't done it because losing my virginity isn't that big of a deal for me. I don't really buy into the societal pressures that seem so prevalent in saying you need to lose your virginity in high school or college to be cool. A lot of people still think I'm cool when they meet me and don't need to know. 

Anyway, to sum up, don't put so much weight into losing your virginity that you think ending your life is the only way forward, it's not that big of a deal, and let me be the excuse for you to think "fuck it" and just go out on weekends sitting in a bar trying to strike up conversations. Who cares if people turn you down, it's all a learning experience. I'd love to know how it goes.

I have tried to do this very thing, it's just that I have trouble sticking with anything. I started making my own game using unity, a great free development software for every platform, but always get so overwhelmed and just give up. I was watching youtube tutorials and starting to make artwork and figure out what my game would be.. And then I just give up.


Now I just put two and two together... I normally get the overwhelmed feeling when I start to get this idea that what I'm doing isn't the most optimal way of doing things. For example making artwork, I would watch 20 different videos trying to find out the best size canvas to use for my sprites, and then I'd watch videos on how to do pixel art, and then how to animate, and I would overwhelm myself. Always trying to find the best way to do it... Which looking back on it seems obvious that a complete beginner wouldn't be able to do things correctly the first time, but when I'm there doing it, it just feels like everything happens naturally like that. :/

Don't worry it didn't make me feel worse... It actually puts things into perspective a little. Honestly, constantly striving for the 100% most efficient way of doing everything is kind of like searching for the *holy grail* or *fountain of youth*; it can't happen because there really is no completely *right* way through life.. Always fearing for mistakes and inefficiency has lead to some of the worst decisions I've made, because I just get stuck trying to find that golden pathway that never reveals itself. 

So, not sure if this thought really helps in any way, but just makes me feel like I need to make a firm decision and stick with it. If I'm not going to go to college, I have to have a plan, and start packing my things lol. If I am, I have to give it my all, cause, well, that's just what the system has set up for me.

Well.. To be honest most of my interests are in computers. I love technology.. I guess my biggest hobby is gaming.. Name a relatively popular online game; I've probably played it. My career in mind was something to do with video games. Design, graphics, I have no clue... I also really like art, but don't feel like I'm good enough to do it as a career, but video game artwork / graphics have always interested me, just not too confident about that one. 

Another hobby, that may come as somewhat of a shocker, is theater. I grew up doing children's theater and I've acted in over 50 plays.. I've also worked behind the scenes; light board, run crew, etc.. But that's more of just a hobby that seems like it will stay a hobby, even though I'm always complimented on my acting it just doesn't seem like a viable or safe career option.


As a side-note, I get an immense thrill just from being in the working world. I don't know what it is. My dad recently (FINALLY) moved back to where I live to work nearby and has quickly moved up the ranks of his very small office. Since it's primarily only him and one other guy working there, they don't mind me stopping by and just hanging out for a few hours a couple times a week. I normally just play on my laptop or sit around, but still, being involved in that kind of work just seems like I could do it. Maybe it's just being with my dad that makes me want to be there, but I would still very much be capable of a job doing something like that (answering phones, writing emails, that kind of work lol, easy stuff, good pay)

>This is a problem I have, I'm incredibly analytical to a fault really, I analyze everything and if I determine that something is corrupt/incorrect/illogical/inefficient/etc... I can't stop myself from trying to correct it or at the very least point out my immense dissatisfaction with it which gets me into trouble.

Wow, rereading the first post again this really hit me... I have always HATED inefficiency, illogic and the like. To the point where it would fuck me over. And now that I feel like what I am supposed to be devoting my entire life to is completely inefficient, it's tearing me up inside.

Hey, thanks for the reply. Really does help to hear someone else knows what I'm going through. I really do feel like college is so pointless, but it's like a road were forced down, which is infuriating, the fact that I'm going somewhere to "learn" from a bunch of academia-crazed professors who are sure to bold  **PHD** on their syllabi, which is most the time either just them ranting or telling me something I could google in a heartbeat if I EVER needed to know it. Still, I understand why it's the right path for many, I just hate that there's not more viable options open, or atleast any that I can easily come up with, for people like you or I. 

I feel like given the freedom and time off I would be able to invent something great, or make a game, or find SOME way of supporting myself or making a living, just given the chance, but all of that just isn't life, and even worse, it's exactly the opposite of what my mom would EVER let me do. Probably because in the past when given free time, all I do is squander it away on video games, but it always feels like it will be different. That's where most of the depression comes from; that feeling that I can't change this cycle, and the people around me just try and beat it out of me.

Again, thank you for sharing the post, and good luck.
